title: Awake, My Soul! Stretch Every Nerve
description: Awake, My Soul! Stretch Every Nerve in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 315, “Forgetting the Things Behind”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-wake, my soul! stretch ev-ery nerve, And press with vig-or on; A heav-enly race de-mands thy zeal, And an im-mor-tal crown.

lines: Awake, my soul! stretch every nerve,
A heavenly race demands thy zeal,
That calls thee from on high;
'Tis His own hand presents the prize
That prize with peerless glories bright,
When victors' wreaths and monarchs' gems

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
